title: Test two upstream pulses and replay a funded chart-552 sink repair
body:
All 32 visible paired-pulse targets fail the immediate one-receipt determinant test. A distinct 336-case causal screen has no joint survivor. A fully replayed grade-five/grade-one funded repair preserves both operators and has complete first-trial BIT margin below −71.651948.

## Scope and source

Extends the fixed-stock #7953 result by changing actual paid upstream payloads. The paired screen fixes other routes and the causal screen has explicitly named arrivals and protected 138. The source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit-sink-upstream-repairs/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. Both cold component replays passed. A separate interpreter checked all 32 determinant cuts and all 680-square forward and adjoint coefficients of the funded word, with corrupted-reader and omitted-XOR controls. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Allow a later replacement receipt or a different genuinely coupled form and retest the complete protected outputs and full invoice.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
